title: schrodinger-fem: a finite element solver for the stationary Schrödinger eigenvalue problem in Elmer
description:
A finite element module for the Elmer package that solves the stationary Schrödinger eigenvalue problem, -nabla^2 psi + V psi = E psi with homogeneous Dirichlet conditions, in one, two and three spatial dimensions.

The weak form yields the generalized symmetric eigenproblem A psi = E M psi with A = K + M_V, assembled with multilinear Lagrange elements. Both a dense route (LAPACK DSYGV) and a sparse route (ARPACK shift-and-invert Arnoldi iteration) are provided; on identical matrices the sparse route is up to 4097 times faster and reduces storage from O(n_f^2) to O(nnz), extending the accessible problem size from about 10^4 to at least 4x10^4 degrees of freedom.

The package also documents two failure modes that are easy to encounter and hard to diagnose. First, the diagonal-shift treatment of Dirichlet data familiar from source problems is invalid for an eigenproblem: it introduces spurious eigenvalues, either at exactly E = 1 or at a distorted value depending on how the mass matrix is treated; the correct procedure eliminates the constrained degrees of freedom, and the accompanying analysis is written in terms of the variational restriction to the free subspace. Second, the module assembles dense local matrices, so all distributed runs return wrong results with more than one rank.

Verification is fourfold: analytic benchmarks across seven cases with smooth and non-smooth potentials, measured convergence orders of O(h^2) for eigenvalues in one, two and three dimensions, code-to-code comparison of two independently written implementations agreeing to about 4x10^-13 in relative terms, and structural invariants including degeneracies, mass-orthonormality and the virial relation.

The deposit contains the Fortran solver module and its build recipe, seven self-contained Elmer benchmark cases with their meshes and input files, the independent Python implementation, the model and solver manuals in English and Portuguese, and the scripts that reproduce every table and figure of the accompanying manuscript. The manuscript itself is published separately and is not part of this deposit.
